question: tools/branches-editor.html, the tool CLAUDE.md tells everyone to use for editing branches.json, carries a full embedded copy of branches.json inside itself as a starting snapshot. options: Make the editor refuse to download until a branches.json has been loaded in that session, so an export can never be built on the snapshot. Smallest change, removes the failure mode entirely, and the snapshot stays useful for read-only browsing
Strip the embedded snapshot out and have the editor open empty with a Load prompt. Removes the stale copy altogether, but the editor stops being a quick way to look at the data without a file to hand

Leave the behaviour alone and keep refreshing the snapshot by hand whenever branches.json changes. No code change, but it depends on every future editor remembering, and the failure is silent when they forget
answer: Recommended option (1): the editor now refuses to Download until a real branches.json has been loaded that session. Answered and implemented directly by Rishi in a Cowork session on 2026-08-09 rather than left for a worker run, since Rishi is stepping away for the next 24 hours and wanted it closed out immediately. Download now checks a loadedFromFile flag, set only by a successful Load; Save shows an explanatory alert and returns early if it is false, instead of silently exporting the bundled snapshot. All five checkers re-run clean afterwards (177 pages, 262 text files, 16 branches, 0 failures).
note: Nothing is blocked by this and nothing about the current data is wrong: the snapshot has been brought level with branches.json as part of this run. It is raised because it is the one route by which a single careless click could undo the whole audit backlog's data work on the single source of truth, and because CLAUDE.md's own rule is that stale copies of branches.json are a hazard. question: Every run today (fourteen local commits now sit ahead of origin/agents/audit-backlog, unchanged at f2fa267; "Host key verification failed" appears eighteen times in AGENT_LOG.md across multiple separate runs) has independently rediscovered that this Cowork sandboxed shell has no working route to GitHub: git@github.com SSH fails host key verification with no ~/.ssh, no gh, no GITHUB_TOKEN and no credential helper present, and anonymous HTTPS only supports reads. Keeps the task running unattended in Cowork as designed, but is a credentials decision, which the worker's own hard rules correctly refuse to make unattended.

Change build-audit-status.js to resolve its repo root relative to the script's own location (e.g. path.join(__dirname, '..')) rather than a hardcoded absolute Windows path, so step 10 at least stops failing identically regardless of host. Leave the sandbox as-is and accept that this task's real output, until someone lands the 14+ queued commits by hand from the native host, is a growing local-only commit history that periodic manual intervention has to push. No infrastructure change, but every future run keeps re-discovering and re-describing the identical blocker at the cost of real run time, as it has at least six times today already.
note: Options 1 and 3 are not mutually exclusive with option 1 - fixing the __dirname path is a small, safe, no-risk code change worth making regardless of where the task ultimately runs, since it is currently wrong on any host that is not exactly C:/Dev/rbh-site-data.
